title: Mac and Cheese
subtitle: Baked macaroni in sharp cheddar bechamel
excerpt: Rigatoni baked in a thick, sharp cheddar sauce with a parmesan crust that bubbles and browns in the oven. The bechamel gets its backbone from toasted and ground mustard seeds, though dry English mustard powder works equally well. This is a proper baked version, not a saucepan quick-fix.
sourceNotes: Mac and cheese has roots in 14th-century Italian pasta dishes; the baked American version was popularised in the 19th century after Thomas Jefferson reportedly served it at a White House dinner.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The whole dish can be assembled, covered and refrigerated up to a day ahead. Add 10 minutes to the bake time if going in cold from the fridge.

content.text: The sauce is the whole point here. Cook the roux until it smells faintly nutty before adding the milk, and let it thicken properly before the cheese goes in. The mustard seeds are toasted and ground in a pestle and mortar; if you have dry English mustard powder, use half a teaspoon of that instead and skip the toasting step. Either way, the mustard sharpens the cheese flavour without tasting of mustard itself.

items.prepNote: toasted in a dry pan then ground; or use 0.5 tsp dry English mustard powder instead

content.text: Heat the oven to 200C (fan 180C / Gas 6). Cook the rigatoni in a large pan of well-salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than the packet says. The pasta will finish cooking in the oven. Drain and set aside.

Melt the butter in the same large pan over a medium heat. Add the flour and stir constantly for 2 minutes until the roux turns a pale biscuit colour and smells slightly nutty. This cooks out the raw flour taste.

Add the warm milk a ladleful at a time, whisking after each addition until smooth before adding the next. Once all the milk is in, cook over a medium-low heat, stirring constantly, for 8 to 10 minutes until the sauce is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.

Remove from the heat. Stir in the ground mustard seeds (or mustard powder), nutmeg and three-quarters of the cheddar. Season well with salt and pepper. Fold in the drained rigatoni until every piece is coated.
Tip into a large baking dish (roughly 30 x 20cm). Scatter the remaining cheddar and all the parmesan over the top. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until bubbling at the edges and deeply golden on top.
Leave to rest for 5 minutes before serving. The sauce will thicken slightly as it cools, which makes it easier to serve in clean portions.

items.cause: The milk was added too quickly or the roux was not smooth before milk was poured in
items.fix: Pass the sauce through a sieve and return to the pan; whisk vigorously over low heat. Next time add milk a little at a time and whisk each addition fully before adding more.

items.cause: Oven temperature too low or the dish was too deep
items.fix: Switch to the grill for the last 3 to 4 minutes, watching closely. Next time spread the pasta shallower in the dish to maximise the crust-to-sauce ratio.
